subject: Residency commitments and question on cross-border/backup processing
messages:
From: Olga Smirnova <olga.smirnova@acme-eu.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Privacy <privacy@acme-eu.com>
Date: 2025-08-21T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Residency assurance and cross-border processing questions

Hi Laura,

Quick set of questions from our legal/privacy review as we look to finalize the SOW and DPA:

1) Does Redwood provide a contractual commitment (in the DPA) to keep Acme customer data and derivatives inside the EU? We need a clear "data residency" clause rather than just an operations note.
2) For the hosted API product (not on-prem), are backups, disaster recovery replicas, or analytics ever replicated outside the EU? If so, what regions and under what contractual authorizations?
3) Where are encryption keys stored/managed for EU-pinned tenants (is KMS/HSM in EU)? Is customer-managed KMS supported?
4) Can you provide the current subprocessors list and indicate which, if any, are outside the EU and what data they process?

We'd like a short paragraph we can insert in our procurement redline that says: "Redwood will not transfer Acme customer data outside the EU except as set forth in Appendix X (disaster recovery/consent)." If you can confirm and point me to the DPA section or a redline we can review, that would help speed approval.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Smirnova
Head of Privacy, Acme Corp (EU)
privacy@acme-eu.com

--
Attachment: none

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Smirnova <olga.smirnova@acme-eu.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-21T10:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and cross-border processing questions

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and a DPA redline attached.

Summary:
- Yes — we offer explicit region-pinning options. For customers requiring EU-only processing we provide an EU-pinned tenancy (hosted) and Redwood Private/Dedicated deployments. The DPA includes language to reflect that pinning and data residency obligations.
- Backups / DR: By default for EU-pinned hostings, backups and DR replicas are kept within the EU. In rare emergency failover cases we reserve the right to temporarily route to an adjacent region; we treat that as an exception subject to the DPA failover appendix.
- KMS: We support EU-based KMS/HSM for EU-pinned customers and also offer customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) via our KMS integrations.
- Subprocessors: see attached CSV for current subprocessors and their regions.

I attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (redline), subprocessors_2025-08-01.csv, SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf.

If you want a one-line procurement-friendly clause to start the redline:
"Redwood will process and store Customer Data in the European Economic Area or in such other countries as agreed in writing; Customer Data will not be transferred outside the EEA except as provided in Appendix X (Emergency Failover) or with Customer's prior written consent."

Would you like us to remove the failover carve-out entirely or add additional controls (notice window, maximum duration)? Happy to loop Legal.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (redline), subprocessors_2025-08-01.csv, SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Olga Smirnova <olga.smirnova@acme-eu.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-21T11:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and cross-border processing questions

Hi Olga — Neha from Legal here. Glad to help clarify the DPA text. A few legal notes and a suggested tightening you can take straight into procurement: 

1) Appendix model: we recommend an Appendix A (Region Pinning) that is incorporated into the DPA by reference. That appendix will identify the Pinning Selection (EEA), permitted exceptions, and the operational controls for backups/DR.
2) Emergency failover carve-out: we can limit this to "temporary failover for a maximum of 72 hours without prior written consent for critical availability events" with an obligation to notify the customer within 4 hours and to provide a remediation report within 7 days. If Acme wants a shorter maximum (e.g., 24 hours) we can discuss, but operationally that constrains some DR vendor processes.
3) Subprocessors: the CSV Laura attached lists subprocessors and their locations. For any subprocessor outside the EEA we can add a commitment to obtain equivalent data protection and to provide 30 days' notice before onboarding; customers can raise objections and we will engage to minimize data exposure.
4) KMS: for EU-pinned customers we will ensure encryption keys for platform-managed keys are stored in EU-HSMs. We also support BYOK where the customer manages the key material (recommended for stricter sovereignty controls).

If you confirm Acme's desired maximum failover duration (24 vs 72 hours) and whether you require BYOK, we'll prepare a procurement-ready DPA redline with the specific Appendix A language and a DocuSign packet.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

--
Attachment references: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessors_2025-08-01.csv

From: Olga Smirnova <olga.smirnova@acme-eu.com>

Cc: Acme Corp Privacy <privacy@acme-eu.com>
Date: 2025-08-21T14:00:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and cross-border processing questions

Thanks Laura and Neha — very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy team:

• Failover window: we need to propose 24 hours maximum for any cross-border failover as a starting point. If you can make that feasible with the notification and remediation commitments, we can accept the carve-out.
• Subprocessors outside EU: please flag which subprocessors (if any) perform any content/derivative analysis or logging outside EU. We are particularly concerned about analytics/telemetry vendors.
• BYOK: Acme wants BYOK for keys used to encrypt customer content; is there any functional limitation we should be aware of?

Also — procurement would like to get the DPA executed this week. Can you send a DocuSign link and confirm the procurement contact we should use?

Thanks,
Olga

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Smirnova <olga.smirnova@acme-eu.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-21T16:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Residency assurance and cross-border processing questions

Hi Olga — great, thanks for the quick response. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Failover window: we can accept 24 hours as the contractual maximum for an emergency cross-border failover, with the following controls: (a) notify Acme within 4 hours of triggering, (b) documented cause and remediation report within 7 days, and (c) restore to EU-pinned infrastructure as soon as reasonably practicable (we've added language to Appendix A in the attached DPA redline).

2) Subprocessors: the attached CSV highlights two analytics/monitoring subprocessors located in the EU and one (Logarithm Analytics Ltd) with EU primary and a US backup environment used only for incident investigation under strict access controls. We will mark that subprocessor in the DPA and offer a 30-day notice before any change.

3) BYOK: supported for EU-pinned customers. No functional limitations for API usage; the primary operational consideration is key rotation windows and the customer having an operational runbook. If Acme wants HSM-backed BYOK, we can support that (we use standard KMS integrations).

4) DocuSign & procurement: DocuSign packet is ready — https://docusign.net/XYZ-ACME-DPA. Please route to procurement@acme-eu.com. HubSpot deal: HS-54321 is updated with the DPA.

Next steps I suggest: (1) procurement confirms BYOK or platform-managed key, (2) Acme confirms acceptance of 24-hour failover window, (3) we send final DocuSign for signature. If you'd like Neha to remove the failover carve-out entirely instead, let us know today.

Thanks again — I'll attach the revised DPA with Appendix A and the subprocessors CSV for your procurement/legal review.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (updated Appendix A), subprocessors_2025-08-01.csv
